subject: Clarify how context summarization and token rounding affect billing / discounts
messages:
From: Jamie Lee <jamie.lee@acme.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Sep 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify billing when we summarize long user histories + discount ask

Hi Vanessa –

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Two follow-ups from the engineering/product team as we scope the pilot:

1) When a user has a long conversation (40+ turns) and our UI asks Redwood to compress older turns into a one-paragraph summary, how do you bill that? Specifically: do you charge for the tokens in the original history that are now summarized, or only for the tokens passed to the model after summarization?

2) We plan to use both streaming responses and periodic non-streamed calls (batched summaries). Does the rounding/minimums policy differ between streaming and non-streaming calls?

3) Commercial—our procurement needs a clear example of how a $50k ARR commit maps to monthly invoiceable tokens, and whether you can make a compression/summary discount part of the pilot.

We've attached a short PDF with the expected conversation distributions and a few sample session lengths. Can someone share one or two worked examples we can show the procurement team?

Appreciate it,
Jamie
Product Partnerships – Acme Health
[Attachment: requirements_summary.pdf (PDF)]

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Jamie Lee <jamie.lee@acme.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Sep 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify billing when we summarize long user histories + discount ask

Hi Jamie —

Summary answers up front:
- We bill for tokens actually sent to the model for inference (input + generated output). If you compress history into a short summary and only send the summary to the model, you are billed for the summary tokens and the model output tokens, not the original full-turn tokens.
- However, there are two practical caveats that affect the invoiceable amount:
  1) Cache-coherency: if the runtime reuses KV cache or prefix cache between calls (same user/session and unchanged prefix), subsequent requests can avoid re-sending identical prefix tokens, which lowers billed input tokens.
  2) Summary generation step: if you request Redwood to generate the summary (i.e., call the model to compress N turns into a summary), that summary generation itself is billed (it consumes tokens during the transform). After that, sending the summary is billed as its own request.

Rounding/minimums:
- For the pilot and typical hosted API usage we currently invoice in 50-token billing quanta after tokenization. Practically, each request's billed token count is rounded to the nearest 50 tokens for invoicing aggregation in that billing window.
- Streaming vs non-streaming: the rounding quantum is the same; streaming calls are measured by the total input+output tokens rounded at the same 50-token quantum. For very small streamed partial outputs we use a 10-token adjustment internally during aggregation, but invoices still reflect the 50-token granularity.

Worked examples (simplified):
A) User with 6-turn history; we generate a 120-token summary from 3,400 tokens of raw history by calling the model to compress. Billing: 3,400 tokens consumed during the compression call (rounded to 3,400 -> 3,400 rounded to nearest 50 = 3,400) + 120 tokens for subsequent inference with the summary (rounded to 150). If you store and reuse the summary across N future calls without regenerating it, future calls only bill the 150 tokens.

B) If you use prefix caching and never regenerate the summary, and your subsequent streaming responses are small (avg 80 tokens output), the typical invoice line per request is ~ (cached input omitted) + output 80 -> rounded to 100.

Commercial options:
- Pilot concession: we can commit to a 20% pilot discount on invoiceable tokens for the first 2 months of the pilot if you sign a short SOW and agree to a usage baseline.
- Commit tiers: 10% discount at $25k/mo committed, 20% at $50k/mo.
- Credit back for over-counting: if we discover any metering mismatch in the first month, we will issue invoice credits (not retroactive rate changes) for confirmed errors.

I'm attaching a simple spreadsheet with worked examples and a sample invoice mapping. Let me know if you want me to turn this into a one-page appendix for your procurement team.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: pricing_model_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Jamie Lee <jamie.lee@acme.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify billing when we summarize long user histories + discount ask

FWIW — a couple of edge cases we should call out explicitly so procurement doesn't raise them later: 

1) Streaming partial outputs followed by a quick follow-up: if the client requests a stream and then immediately requests a continuation that re-sends the same prompt prefix, we currently dedupe prefixes at the runtime layer in many cases, but deduplication isn't guaranteed cross-region or across some Dedicated configurations. For invoicing, we treat the requests as separate calls unless prefix dedupe is observed in telemetry.

2) When summaries are generated server-side as a background job (e.g., nightly stitching), that cost is billed to the customer who owns the workspace that triggered the job. If Acme wants us to absorb nightly stitching compute for the pilot, we can scope that as a cost concession in the SOW.

Example calc from Vanessa's sheet (pulled out):
- Summarize 3,400 tokens -> summary 120 tokens. Compression call billed: 3,400 (rounded to 3,400). Subsequent 12 queries using that summary where output avg 80 tokens each -> per call bill 100 tokens (rounded) -> 12 * 100 = 1,200. Total pilot window = 3,400 + 1,200 = 4,600 tokens.

Can we add a short paragraph in the SOW appendix that defines "summary generation" vs "summary usage" so finance has the language?

- Ben
Director, Sales Engineering

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jamie Lee <jamie.lee@acme.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Oct 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify billing when we summarize long user histories + discount ask

Thanks team — commercial proposal we can take to Acme procurement: 

1) Pilot package: 60-day pilot with a $10k invoice cap for the pilot period and a 20% usage discount applied to invoiceable tokens (as Vanessa proposed).
2) Metering appendix: explicit language that differentiates (A) "summary generation" (charged at actual tokens consumed when model creates the summary), (B) "summary usage" (charged for tokens in the summary and subsequent outputs), and (C) "cached prefix reuse" (excluded from future billed input when cache reuse is confirmed).
3) Rounding: round invoiceable tokens to the nearest 50 tokens per billing period. If we discover an internal metering mismatch > 1% across the pilot, Redwood issues a credit for the difference.
4) Commercial concession: if Acme signs a 12-month commit of $50k+/mo within 30 days of pilot completion, extend an additional 5% discount on top of tiered pricing for the next 12 months.

Jamie — can you confirm procurement will accept a capped pilot invoice and the proposed SOW appendix language? If yes, I'll get Legal to prepare a short SOW and send to Acme Contracts.

Marissa
Sr. VP, Sales — Redwood Inference

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Jamie Lee <jamie.lee@acme.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 02 Oct 2026 15:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify billing when we summarize long user histories + discount ask

Thanks all — Jamie, sounds good from our side if procurement agrees. Quick confirmation and next steps: 

- We will treat summary generation as a billable transform step and clearly distinguish it in the SOW appendix.
- Invoice rounding: nearest 50 tokens per billing period (will include sample calculations).
- Pilot concession: 20% discount for first 60 days, $10k invoice cap for the pilot period.
- If you hit the commit threshold ($50k/mo) within 30 days of pilot close, we'll apply the additional 5% offer for 12 months.

I've asked Legal to prepare SOW_v1 with the appendix language and will loop Acme Contracts. Attaching the redline we will send — please review and flag any language you want tightened (esp. the meter reconciliation clause).

Links: HubSpot deal and DocuSign SOW will follow when Legal publishes.

Cheers,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
